transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [name]. Thank you for seeing me. I... well, honestly, I don't even exactly know where to start, but I guess I'm here because things have gotten to a point where I'm actually frightening myself. I work as a veterinary technologist, which I usually love, I mean I went to grad school for this, I've been doing it a long time. I'm 52 now, so I'm very used to the stress and the long hours at the clinic and dealing with the animals and the owners. But lately, everything just feels so impossibly heavy. 

I try to just push through it, but what really pushed me to pick up the phone, what genuinely scared me enough to come in, is that I keep having these thoughts. I go to bed after a long shift and I just keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. Just... peace, you know? No more waking up to do it all over again. And then, it bleeds into the day, too. Sometimes when I’m driving home from the clinic, especially on this one really sharp curve on my route where the speed limit drops, I actually catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn’t turn the wheel. If I just let my hands stay perfectly still and let the car go straight off the road. I snap out of it, and my heart starts pounding, but the fact that my brain is even going there... it's just terrifying me. I can't keep living with my mind doing this.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did these low mood and these thoughts about not waking up first start?

Well, it’s not like a switch just flipped overnight, you know? It’s been... gosh, it’s been hanging over me for a really long time now. I’d say about 11 months? Yes, nearly a year of just dragging myself out of bed and forcing myself to put on my scrubs and pretend everything is fine for the animals and the pet owners. For those first ten months or so, it was just this constant, heavy, dark cloud. I was drained, just absolutely exhausted to my bones, but I could still kind of function, or at least fake it well enough that my coworkers didn't pull me aside to ask what was wrong. I just kept telling myself it was burnout, that I just needed a vacation or a long weekend, but no amount of rest actually helped. 

But then... this past month. This past month has just been a completely different level of awful. It’s like whatever tiny reserves I had left just completely evaporated, and everything became genuinely unbearable. That's when it went from just feeling terribly low all the time to actually having those horrible thoughts about not waking up, or staring at the steering wheel on my commute. So the depression itself, that heavy feeling, that’s been there for about 11 months, but this terrifying, unbearable part? That’s really been the last four weeks or so. It just feels like it's never going to end, and I keep trying to trace it back to what started it all 11 months ago, but I just don't know. It just crept in and never left, and now it's just so heavy I can barely breathe under it.

Have you ever, at any other time in your life, gone through a period of days or weeks where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or took on risky or impulsive behavior that was out of character for you?

It’s... it's actually really strange that you ask that, because yes. Just earlier this month, actually. Which is so confusing because I've been so incredibly drained for the past year, but there was this stretch where I felt... I don't know, almost electrically upbeat? Like there was this buzzing, restless energy right under my skin. I was just humming with it. But it wasn't a good feeling, because it would just twist, almost instantly, into this intense, fiery irritability. 

I am normally a very patient person. You really have to be in vet med, you know? The animals can't tell you what's wrong, the owners are usually terrified or stressed out, and you're constantly adapting to chaos. I've done this for decades, I know how to keep my cool. But earlier this month, I was just snapping at everyone over the absolute tiniest, most insignificant things. I remember one of the newer assistants misplaced a medication cup—literally just a little plastic dosing cup, we have hundreds of them in the supply closet, it does not matter at all—and I just completely lost it on her. I felt my chest get all tight and I just chewed her out in front of the treatment room. 

And then, I think it was the very next day, there was a slight change in the morning schedule. Which happens every single day! It's the nature of the job, an emergency HBC—hit by car—comes in, and you have to bump a routine spay or neuter. You just roll with it. But when the receptionist told me about the schedule change, I snapped at her, too. I was practically biting her head off over a fifteen-minute delay. It really, really didn’t feel like my usual self at all. I remember standing by the centrifuge afterward, just vibrating with this weird, angry, electric energy, thinking, "Who is this person?" Because it's just not me to act like that over a plastic cup or a schedule shift. I usually pride myself on being the anchor when the clinic gets crazy, but I just couldn't stop myself from lashing out, and I... I don't know where that came from, it was just so strange...

That period of feeling wired, irritable, and full of restless energy—how many days in a row did it last, and were you also feeling deeply depressed and having those thoughts about not waking up during that very same time?

Well, it was... gosh, it lasted for exactly four days. I remember it so clearly because it started on a Tuesday and finally sort of broke on Friday evening. And yes, that's the thing that is just so incredibly confusing and awful about it—I was having those terrible, dark thoughts at the exact same time. It’s like my brain was a car with one foot slamming on the gas and the other one slamming on the brakes. I was so exhausted and having these terrifying thoughts about just letting the car drift off the road, but at the same time, I had all this... this buzzing, frantic energy that I just didn't know what to do with. 

I mean, normally, when I get home from a long shift at the clinic, especially lately, I just collapse. I sink into the couch and I don't move. But during those four days, I couldn't sit still to save my life. I’d get home, and instead of resting, I just started pacing. Pacing back and forth through the house, up and down the hallway, into the living room, into the kitchen. I couldn't stop moving. And then I started measuring things. I don't even know why! I grabbed a tape measure from the junk drawer and I just started measuring the dimensions of the rooms, writing them down on these little notepads. I was making these huge, elaborate lists of things I thought I needed to do, or projects I should start, even though I had absolutely no real intention of doing them. 

And then I started on the cabinets. My husband had already gone to bed—he usually goes to sleep around 10:30 because he has an early start—and I was just wide awake in the kitchen at, like, 1:00 in the morning, completely emptying out the pantry and the dish cabinets. I was wiping down the shelves, reorganizing the canned goods by expiration date and alphabetical order, matching all the Tupperware lids to the containers... which, honestly, is a nightmare on a good day, but I was just frantically doing it in the middle of the night. I was so tired, so deeply, painfully sad, just wishing I wouldn't wake up the next morning, but my body just kept going and going and going. It was like I was trapped in this horrible, high-speed nightmare for those four days.
Right now, today, are you having any thoughts of ending your life, and if so, have you thought about a specific plan or taken any steps toward acting on it?

Honestly, right now... today... it's just so hard to even say it out loud. But yes. I am. I don't have a... a specific, detailed plan, like I haven't written a note or gone out and bought anything, I haven't taken any actual steps like that. I haven't done anything to prepare. But what really scared me enough to finally come in here and talk to you is that I just keep thinking, almost constantly now, that it would be so much easier if I just didn’t wake up. Like, if I could just go to sleep tonight and that would be it, no more dragging myself through the days, no more pretending for the staff or the clients. Just quiet. 

And the really frightening part, the thing that made me realize I couldn't just keep ignoring this and blaming it on burnout, happens on my commute. I have this drive home from the clinic, it’s about thirty minutes, mostly on this winding two-lane county road, and I’m usually so drained I drive it on autopilot. But lately... I catch myself just staring at the road ahead, especially when I'm coming up to a sharp curve, and I catch myself wondering what would happen if I didn’t turn the wheel. Just... what if I kept my hands completely still and let the car drift right off the pavement and into the trees? I grip the steering wheel so tight when it happens because it genuinely terrifies me that my brain is even going there. I've driven that road for years, and now it feels like a hazard just because of my own mind. So, no, I haven't made a concrete plan to do it, but those thoughts of just letting the car drift, or just hoping I don't wake up tomorrow... they are right there, even today.
